notes: Local corrections of the generated land where the frozen 2023 USGS raster predates what was built (tools/lib/terrain-overrides.mjs). World metres: +X east, +Z south.

A site's scope is its OSM areas plus traced polygons (add_xz), minus corridors round protected ways (exclude_ways) and traced polygons (exclude_xz), inside the land. The correction fades to exactly zero over edge_blend_m at the scope's edge, so the land outside the scope and on the coastline keeps its generated surface.

The site's grade is a harmonic membrane on a grid_m grid (relaxation over-relaxation factor, a fixed number of iterations): it takes the generated land outside the scope and the level and profile targets inside their shapes, and is as smooth as possible everywhere else, so the 32 m land grid's waves smooth out and designed surfaces meet their surroundings in gentle ramps. Regions apply in order: level holds a flat elevation_m inside its shape, profile holds control elevations_m along its line, sink cuts depth_m below the grade with a smoothstep rim side_run_m wide. Shapes: points_xz (optionally grown by buffer_m, negative to inset), line_xz with width_m, or an ellipse (center_xz, radii_m, rotation_deg turning +X toward +Z).

Every 32 m land cell the correction reaches is re-meshed as a quadtree of leaves down to min_leaf_m, split until each leaf's two triangles stay within tolerance_m of the corrected surface (sampled every sample_m); shared edges stay watertight, coarse neighbours keep their surface.
All elevations, depths and rims here are production inference for game art, traced from the designer's plan and dated photos, not survey data.

sites.name: 9th Street and Avenue H construction site
sites.evidence: Large-clutter place #12 (OSM w775820811 landuse=construction). The scope reaches 16 m past the Job Corps fence on the site's west side, where the 32 m land grid smears the stockpile's flank; 449 Avenue H (w34313512) and the streets stay outside it. Strips 3 m wide straddle every edge of the OSM area, so the traced bands and the area overlap instead of leaving slivers; the land cell beside 516 Avenue H (w110188516) is levelled too, and a sliver of that building's own cell (between Avenue H and its west wall) joins the scope so its foundation is re-cut from the re-meshed facets rather than split around. Pits from the May 2026 aerial are cut 1 m into the levelled site (owner-approved levelling, 2026-11-04; review round 3, 2026-11-04).

sites.name: Hangar earthworks pad
sites.evidence: Large-clutter place #11 (inside OSM w1252737732 landuse=construction). Esri World Imagery, Vantor capture 2026-05-26 (large-clutter research tile t-southeast, 0.6 m) shows a flat, pale graded pad closed by a ring of black-plastic berms, the old embankment on its south-east side and shallow ponds at its west end; the 2023 USGS raster still holds the stockpiles that were graded since (the pad reads 2.4 to 10.6 m there). The pad and the ring's north-west, north, north-east and south-west sides are levelled to 2.8 m, the pad's own grade (the median of the raster inside it); the south-east embankment (to about 11 m) stays as the ring's base, its inner slope cut back to the band's edge in the aerial, the scope reaching 14 m into it so the grade ramps up gently under the plastic. The hangars (Buildings 2 and 3), the Job Corps grounds (the scope stops 1.5 m inside their fence, w1252737750) and the streets stay outside it, and so does every 32 m land cell beside a building (the pad's west corner and south-west side among them), so no foundation is re-cut. Owner-approved levelling 2026-11-04; review round 3, 2026-11-04.

sites.name: Avenue M beside the concrete recycling yard
sites.evidence: Large-clutter place #7. The 32 m land grid smears the yard's rubble mound (the 2023 USGS raster, about 11 m) out over its Avenue M wall line and Avenue M itself, which rise 3-7 m there; Google Street View, 92 Avenue M, Nov 2025 (camera x 525, z 154, heading 64) shows Avenue M flat and the double-stacked container wall standing at street level with the rubble only just showing over it. Google Street View, 3rd St, Mar 2025 (camera x 598, z 170, heading 354) shows the 3rd St wall standing at street level near the south corner, the rubble mound behind it. Avenue M and the strip inside the wall are levelled to the street's grade (4.0 m), and the 3rd St wall's base with them, stepping down 0.2 m to 3rd St's own 3.8 m past the smear; the mound inside rises from behind the wall as the raster has it, the ramp from the wall base fading into the kept mound over 10 m so that no face is steeper than 48 degrees. Land cells beside buildings stay unsplit (so no foundation is re-cut). Owner-approved levelling 2026-11-05 (as the #12 and Cityside Park corrections).

sites.name: Avenue M staging yard's soil mound and plastic stockpile
sites.evidence: Large-clutter place #9 (inside OSM w899364786 landuse=construction). The 2023 USGS raster is flat here (3.0-3.6 m). Esri World Imagery, Vantor capture 2026-05-26 (0.5 m island tile and large-clutter research tile z-ne-yard, 0.25 m) shows a tan soil mound about 65 by 65 m (x 585-650, z 165-230) with an excavator and a truck on it, and east of it, between 3rd St and Avenue N, a black-plastic-covered stockpile about 45 m wide at its north end, tapering over 90 m; Google Street View, 22 Avenue M, Nov 2025 (camera x 587, z 271, heading 54) shows the big mound behind the yard's screened fence with an excavator working on top. Owner-approved 2026-11-05.
